title: Gemma 4 Technical Report
data_curation: Pretraining data is a large, diverse mix of web documents, code, images and audio (audio only for E2B, E4B and 12B), with a January 2025 cutoff. It is filtered to decontaminate benchmarks and to reduce unsafe utterances and recitation, and personal and sensitive information is removed. The tokenizer is Gemini's SentencePiece tokenizer (262k vocabulary, split digits, preserved whitespace, byte-level fallback). For post-training, the report filters out examples showing certain personal information, unsafe or toxic outputs, mistaken self-identification, and duplicates. It adds subsets that encourage in-context attribution, hedging and refusals, which improve factuality without hurting other metrics. No dataset sizes, sources or reward/verifier designs are given for the instruction-tuning data.
curriculum: The pipeline is pretraining followed by instruction tuning, both 'similar to Gemma 3'. The one stated post-training difference is the new thinking mode. The report does not describe stage ordering, SFT/RL splits, mixing ratios or schedules. Vision and audio encoders are frozen during pretraining. The 12B model is trained from scratch in a new encoder-free setup. Quantization-aware training produces mobile (int2/int4 weights, int8 activations) and Q4_0 checkpoints, and QAT is also applied to the encoders (W8A8 for the 150M vision encoder; 2/4/8-bit weights for the audio encoder). Training runs on TPUv4/v6e (4,096–12,288 chips) with ZeRO-3, Pathways, GSPMD and Slice-Granularity Elasticity.
method: The family has dense E2B (2.3B effective / 5B total, with per-layer embeddings), E4B (4.5B / 8B), 12B and 31B models, plus a 26B-A4B MoE (3.8B active). Attention interleaves local and global layers at 5:1 (4:1 for E2B). Global layers use p-RoPE (p=0.25, base 1M) and reuse keys as values (except E2B/E4B); local layers use RoPE with base 10k. KV is shared across layers at 20/35 (E2B) and 18/42 (E4B). Together these cut the global KV cache by up to 37.5%. Vision uses ViT encoders (150M or 550M, patch 16, aspect-ratio-preserving resize, N_max of 70–1120 tokens). Audio uses a 305M USM-Conformer encoder, 55% smaller than Gemma 3n's. The encoder-free 12B projects 48×48 RGB patches through one 35M matmul and raw 640-dimensional 40ms audio chunks directly into the LLM. An autoregressive MTP drafter (4-layer Transformer cross-attending to the main model's KV) supports speculative decoding. The thinking trace is emitted in a <|channel>thought…<channel|> block and toggled with <|think|>.
eval_metrics: Human evaluation is Arena Text Elo. Static benchmarks are reported mostly in thinking mode and cover MMLU Pro, AIME 2026 without tools, LiveCodeBench v6, Codeforces Elo, SciCode, GPQA Diamond, BBEH, HLE (with and without search), IFBench, IFEval, MMMLU, MRCR v2 8-needle at 128k, Terminal Bench Hard, and Tau2 (airline, retail, telecom). Vision uses MMMU Pro, MATH-Vision, MedXPertQA MM, InfographicVQA and OmniDocBench 1.5. Audio uses CoVoST BLEU and FLEURS WER/CER. Long context uses RULER, LOFT, GraphWalks and MTOB (up to ~256k). Headline numbers for the 31B model: MMLU Pro 85.2, AIME 2026 89.2, LiveCodeBench 80.0, Codeforces 2150, GPQA 84.3, HLE 19.5, IFEval 98.9, Tau2-retail 86.4, and RULER-128k 96.4 (vs 66.0 for Gemma 3 27B).
key_results: Gemma 4 31B scores 1451 Elo on Arena Text, the top dense open model, close to far larger MoEs such as DeepSeek V4 Pro (1456). The 26B-A4B scores 1438, vs 1366 for Gemma 3 27B. The 31B lifts AIME 2026 from 20.8 to 89.2 and Codeforces Elo from 110 to 2150 over Gemma 3 27B. On audio, E2B/E4B improve over Gemma 3n by 12%/10% on translation and 17%/12% on ASR with a 78% smaller encoder.
evolution_note: Gemma 4 succeeds Gemma 2/3 and Gemma 3n, reusing Gemma 3's local:global attention recipe and Gemma 3n's per-layer embeddings and USM audio encoder. Its main post-training addition is an o1-style thinking mode, which brings the open Gemma line into the reasoning-model era. The report's other contributions are efficiency work: K=V global layers, p-RoPE, KV sharing, MTP drafters, QAT and an encoder-free 12B. The post-training recipe itself is barely documented, so the report is more useful as an efficient-architecture reference than as a post-training recipe.
